record.paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
record.original_question: Let X be a separable Banach space such that every separable Banach space is Lipschitz isomorphic to a subset of X. Must X contain a copy of c_0?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. (Converse Aharoni problem – see [11, 44]) Let X be a separable Banach space with the property that every separable Banach space is Lipschitz iso￾morphic to a subset of X. Is it true that X contains a copy of c0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $c_0$ denote the Banach space of real sequences converging to zero, equipped with the supremum norm. A map $f:(M,d_M)\to(N,d_N)$ between metric spaces is a Lipschitz isomorphism onto its image if there exist constants $0<a\le b<\infty$ such that $a\,d_M(x,y)\le d_N(f(x),f(y))\le b\,d_M(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in M$. By Aharoni's theorem, every separable metric space is Lipschitz isomorphic to a subset of $c_0$.

Suppose $X$ is a separable Banach space with the following universality property: every separable Banach space $Y$ is Lipschitz isomorphic to some subset of $X$. Must $X$ contain a closed linear subspace isomorphic to $c_0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The converse Aharoni problem—whether a separable Banach space into which every separable Banach space (or equivalently $c_0$) Lipschitz-embeds must contain an isomorphic copy of $c_0$—is reported as still open in surveys on the nonlinear geometry of Banach spaces. Partial results exist (e.g., subspaces of $c_0$ are stable under Lipschitz isomorphism, and any Banach space Lipschitz isomorphic to $c_0$ is linearly isomorphic to it), but the general question remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A short course on non linear geometry of Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the nonlinear geometry of Banach spaces, discussing the converse Aharoni problem and related open questions about Lipschitz embeddings into c_0.
status_evidence.claim: The converse Aharoni problem is listed among open problems in the nonlinear geometry of Banach spaces.

status_evidence.title: Subspaces of c_0(N) and Lipschitz isomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that the class of subspaces of c_0 is stable under Lipschitz isomorphism; a Banach space Lipschitz isomorphic to c_0 is linearly isomorphic to c_0.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: rigidity of c_0 under Lipschitz isomorphisms, but the converse Aharoni problem itself remains open.
